title: SOCATA TB 20 Trinidad — Emergency Procedures
description: Emergency procedures for the SOCATA TB 20 Trinidad with Lycoming IO-540 fuel-injected engine, constant-speed propeller, and retractable tricycle gear. Memory items are marked. The IO-540 is fuel-injected — carburetor ice does not apply to the induction system, but intake icing is noted where relevant. The TB 20 has a manual emergency gear extension system; locate and review the override mechanism before flight. All airspeeds and numerical limits must come from the specific aircraft POH. These procedures are a general guide only — not a substitute for recurrent emergency training or a qualified type checkout.

source.notes: No manufacturer document consulted. Written from general familiarity with the type.

known_issues.description: Contains no airspeeds, power settings, fuel quantities, or other numerical limitations — all must come from the specific aircraft POH.
Equipment variations exist across this model/variant. Verify items against the specific aircraft before use.

rights.notes: Manufacturer POH remains under copyright. This file does not reproduce its wording or selection of items.

sections.title: Engine Failure on Takeoff — Before or At Liftoff

items.text: Throttle
Brakes — apply firmly to stop within remaining runway length

Ignition switch
Master switch
Fuel selector
Do not attempt a turn back to the runway at low altitude. If airborne with insufficient runway remaining, land ahead or on the best available surface within a narrow arc of the departure heading.
Occupants — advise to brace for impact
Airspeed — pitch for best glide without delay
Landing area — identify best available field or surface within glide range
Fuel selector — switch to opposite tank
Mixture
Ignition switch
Electric fuel pump
Throttle — advance if restart is being attempted
If restart fails — secure engine and follow Forced Landing checklist

items.response: IDLE CUTOFF — starve fire of fuel

items.text: Fuel selector
Throttle
items.response: FULL OPEN — clear residual fuel from induction system

items.text: Electric fuel pump
Master switch
Airspeed — increase if fire persists to attempt to blow out flames; do not exceed Vne
If fire extinguishes — execute immediate precautionary landing; do not attempt restart
If fire continues — execute forced landing with urgency; follow Forced Landing checklist
Mixture
Ignition switch
Fuel selector
Master switch
Occupants — evacuate immediately via car-style doors; move upwind of the aircraft
Fire extinguisher — direct at base of fire through cowl openings if accessible without risk
Emergency services — call 911 / ATC / airport fire
Master switch
Avionics master switch
Vents and fresh air — open to ventilate cabin; do not fan smouldering materials
If smoke and fire subside — identify and isolate the faulty circuit before restoring power
Essential avionics — restore selectively and one at a time; monitor for recurrence
items.response: RESTORED AS NEEDED FOR SAFE FLIGHT

items.text: Land as soon as practicable
Oil pressure gauge — confirm reading and crosscheck oil temperature for trend
Power — reduce to minimum required to maintain safe flight
Land as soon as possible — do not operate with low or zero oil pressure; total engine failure may follow
Suitable landing area — identify in case of sudden engine seizure
ATC — declare emergency and advise intentions
If engine seizes — follow Engine Failure in Flight checklist

The IO-540 is fuel-injected — carburetor ice does not occur. However, impact icing of the primary air inlet is possible in visible moisture. The TB 20 is equipped with an alternate air source; activation bypasses the primary induction inlet.
Symptoms — rough running, loss of power, or unusual RPM/MAP fluctuation in IMC or visible moisture
Alternate air control — select ALTERNATE AIR (or ALT AIR OPEN per aircraft labelling)
Engine performance — monitor for recovery; expect slight power reduction on alternate air
Altitude and routing — avoid continued flight in icing conditions if practical
If power does not recover — treat as engine emergency and prepare for precautionary landing
Airspeed — establish and maintain best glide
Landing area — select the best available surface; commit and do not change plan at low altitude
Transponder
ATC — declare MAYDAY; state position, altitude, and intentions
Fuel selector
Mixture
Ignition switch
Master switch — leave on until final approach to retain flap and gear operation, then OFF
Flaps — extend on final approach per POH to reduce touchdown speed
Landing gear — extend if landing on a prepared surface; leave retracted for off-field terrain landing per judgement
items.response: DOWN FOR PAVED/FIRM SURFACE; CONSIDER RETRACTED FOR ROUGH TERRAIN

items.text: Seat belts and shoulder harnesses — all occupants confirm tight
Doors — unlatch before touchdown to prevent jamming

sections.title: Gear Unsafe / Gear Will Not Indicate Down

items.text: Gear handle — confirm in DOWN position
Airspeed — confirm within gear operating speed range
Circuit breakers — check gear-related breakers for tripped condition
items.response: BREAKERS CHECKED; RESET IF TRIPPED ONCE

items.text: Gear handle — recycle: raise then lower again
If still unsafe — fly-by or request tower visual inspection if available
If gear will not extend normally — proceed to Emergency Gear Extension checklist

Locate and review the manual gear extension mechanism in the specific aircraft before flight. Mechanism location and procedure vary by aircraft serial and modification status — always verify against the aircraft POH.
Airspeed — reduce to below maximum gear extension speed and maintain
items.response: AT OR BELOW Vlo PER POH

items.text: Landing gear handle
Gear circuit breaker — check and reset if tripped
Emergency gear extension — engage manual override per aircraft POH procedure
Gear position indicators — verify three green after manual extension
items.response: THREE GREEN CONFIRMED — OR NOTE ANY UNSAFE INDICATION

items.text: If any gear does not show green — do not retract; plan for minimum runway landing; notify ATC
items.response: ATC ADVISED; EMERGENCY DECLARED IF NOT ALREADY

items.text: After landing — do not taxi; shutdown on runway and await maintenance inspection before any further movement
items.response: AIRCRAFT STOPPED ON RUNWAY; MAINTENANCE NOTIFIED
